events.title: Inside India newsletter: Trump's poll setback fuels hope for U.S.-India trade deal by year end
events.summary: After the loss in the midterm polls, U.S. President Donald Trump is keener to make a trade announcement, and India is the most likely candidate. Democrats are mounting pressure on Trump's tariff policies. The trade deal could be signed in December, on the sidelines of the G20 summit in December, where Modi and Trump will be present, experts said. Hello, this is Priyanka Salve, writing to you from India. Welcome to the latest edition of " Inside India " — your one-stop destination for stories and developments from the world's fastest-growing large economy. After months of being weighed down by high energy prices, trade uncertainty and foreign investor exodus, India has had plenty to celebrate this Diwali. Foreign investors returned to its market in November and, now, it seems the long-awaited U.S.-India trade deal could be around the corner. Experts say that the two sides are closer to signing on the dotted line following the U.S. midterm election results than they were before. Any thoughts on today's newsletter? Share them with the team. The U.S.-India trade deal, which has been riddled with uncertainty since February, is likely to get a final push to the finish line, thanks to U.S. President Donald Trump's electoral setback in the midterm polls. Experts told CNBC that Trump could lean toward closing some of the pending trade deals to promote them as policy achievements to the American public, and the pact with New Delhi is a "prime candidate." They added that Trump and Indian Prime Minister Modi are likely to sign the trade pact when they meet in December for the G20 leaders meeting, as negotiations have largely concluded. The U.S.-India trade talks "are far along and there seems to be a gentlemen's agreement between Trump and Modi" that the deal should be concluded when the two meet at Mar-a-Lago in December, Mark Linscott, former assistant U.S. trade representative and senior advisor at the U.S.-India Strategic Partnership Forum, told CNBC. Trump has used tariffs as a pressure tactic to clinch trade deals with several countries, even as that approach has drawn the ire of his political opponents who have flagged that export levies have increased costs for American households. Cost of living was the top concern for American voters in the midterms. "The election was a verdict on the cost of living, and tariffs are now a liability the President cannot defend on the numbers," Ronak D. Desai, visiting fellow at Hoover Institution of Stanford University, told CNBC. "Congress will not hand him an affordability win, but a trade deal is one he can announce on his own," Desai said, adding that an announcement of a deal with India is "more likely than it was before the election." India's commerce and external affairs ministries and the U.S. Trade Representative's Office did not respond to CNBC's requests for comment. When asked about how U.S. midterm election results will reshape the ties with New Delhi, a spokesperson for India's Ministry of External Affairs on Tuesday said that the relationship between the two countries " enjoys bipartisan support in the United States." Trump insists Americans do not share the burden of his tariffs, but according to estimates from Tax Foundation, a nonprofit, the duties raised the average U.S. household's tax burden by $820 in 2026 and $1,000 in 2025. As a result, the Democrats, within days of taking control of both the houses of Congress are preparing to challenge Trump's signature tariff policy. A trade deal at this time could be seen as a validation of Trump's tariffs-led approach to business. "The president may lean more into getting deals done – seeing them as policy achievements that he can promote to the American public," Atman Trivedi, partner at Washington-based DGA Albright Stonebridge Group, told CNBC. He added that the Trump administration would like to get a deal done with India by the G20 leaders' summit in December. While American voters are more affected by import duties on Canadian goods, experts said that a trade deal with India could blunt criticism about tariffs as an effective bargaining chip. In February, Trump announced a deal with India, claiming that New Delhi had agreed to "Buy American" at a much higher level after the U.S. agreed to slash tariffs to 18%. Trump had earlier imposed a 25% tariff on imports from India, along with an additional 25% duty on goods from New Delhi for buying Russian oil. But that deal has since been awaiting final approval, especially after the Supreme Court struck down Trump tariffs, giving India space to demand preferential tariffs that give it an edge over competitors. While American and Indian officials at the start of October said that the negotiations had reached an impasse , Trump on Oct. 20 said that the two sides were " pretty close " to a final deal. As per Indian media reports, the country's Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal confirmed that discussions on the trade deal had largely "concluded.

events.title: Nvidia's succession dilemma just got real. Here's who could take over if Jensen Huang steps down.
events.summary: 21 October 2026, Berlin: Jensen Huang, co-founder and CEO of Nvidia, speaks during GTC Berlin. The U.S. chipmaker held its AI conference from October 20 to 22, 2026. Photo: Soeren Stache/dpa (Photo by Soeren Stache/picture alliance via Getty Images) Soeren Stache/picture alliance via Getty Images Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's admission of an affair and a board investigation has sparked questions about succession. The board is reportedly discussing removing Huang after a report of a second romance with a direct report. Analysts and former employees point to Colette Kress and Ian Buck as possible successors. It's hard to imagine Nvidia without Jensen Huang — and the CEO has repeatedly discussed his intention to work for as long as possible. Now, the question of succession has come into sharp focus after Huang admitted to having one affair, Nvidia's board announced it's investigating whether Huang was the target of a "foreign intelligence effort," and The New York Times reported he also had a romance with a direct report at Nvidia. If Huang steps down or is ousted from his role, analysts and former employees floated several potential successors, including vice president Ian Buck and chief financial officer Colette Kress. Huang's two children, Madison and Spencer, also work at Nvidia, raising questions about whether leadership could remain in the family. Nvidia told Business Insider in a statement on Sunday that "Jensen is committed to continuing to lead Nvidia as CEO without interruption." On Wednesday, after the bombshell report that Huang had an affair with executive Kimberly Powell, The Wall Street Journal reported that the board was preparing to remove Huang. Huang would be hard to replace, said Brad Gastwirth, the global head of research at Circular Technology. While Huang doesn't have controlling voting power, he owns about 3.6% of Nvidia and would likely "have considerable input into succession unless the investigation uncovers serious wrongdoing," Gastwirth said. "Jensen's combination of technical expertise, strategic vision, and industry relationships is nearly impossible to replicate," he said. Inside Nvidia's succession dilemma Nvidia has not publicly designated a number two, and Huang is known for keeping an unusually flat leadership structure with as many as 60 direct reports . "That works beautifully while he's in the seat, but it means nobody has been groomed, tested, or publicly positioned as the heir," said Daniel Newman, CEO of The Futurum Group. One former employee said Madison Huang, who works as senior director of product marketing for physical AI, has been asserting greater authority across Nvidia's businesses, which they believe could be an effort to position herself for a larger leadership role. Madison Huang, Jensen Huang's daughter and Nvidia's senior director of product marketing for physical AI. Bloomberg/Getty Images Gil Luria, an analyst at DA Davidson, said Kress is the company's only other highly visible executive and could take over as interim CEO if Huang stepped aside. Kress has worked at Nvidia for 13 years, and prior to that, she held finance roles at Cisco and Microsoft. Colette Kress, chief financial officer of Nvidia. Nvidia Since Kress lacks the engineering background that has been central to Huang's leadership, another possible long-term replacement is Ian Buck , a longtime executive who helped develop CUDA, the chip software that has become central to Nvidia's dominance in AI. Buck heads Nvidia's data center and computing businesses, and he has worked at Nvidia for 22 years. "He's already running the group that is generating virtually all the revenues," the former employee said, referring to Nvidia's data center business. Ian Buck, vice president of accelerated computing at Nvidia. David Paul Morris/Bloomberg via Getty Images Dan Morgan, vice president at Synovus Trust Company, said that Nvidia cofounder and fellow Chris Malachowsky could be a key player in a leadership change. Huang and Malachowsky cofounded Nvidia along with Curtis Priem. "He may be a part of the leadership change if Huang steps down," Morgan wrote in a note to investors. "Despite Huang's ownership stake, I would still assume as a founder, to heavily influence the succession decision." A second former employee cited the importance of Nvidia's distinctive culture in promoting a current executive as a successor. "Ideally it has to be someone from the company who's lived the values and the culture," they said. Could Nvidia look to an outsider? Some observers have floated executives from other major technology companies as potential successors, including Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian and Amazon Web Services CEO Matt Garman. Both oversee enormous cloud computing businesses that invest heavily in AI infrastructure and work closely with Nvidia, giving them firsthand knowledge of the customers and technologies driving its growth. While Huang's departure appears unlikely for now, Gastwirth said losing him under the current circumstances could seriously hurt Nvidia. "I think it would be one of the worst things that could happen to Nvidia," he said. "The company would continue operating, but I would question whether it could maintain the same pace of innovation and execution." Have a tip? events.title: Personal data stolen after National Parks booking service hacked in three states
events.summary: News Home Just In For You Analysis Rural Watch Live Health Indigenous Politics Science Deep Time Elections World Environment Investigations Business Local news Quizzes Sport AFL NRL Football Tennis Cricket Netball Lifestyle Wellbeing Relationships & Family Food & Recipes Personal Finance Home & Garden Entertainment TV & Movies Books Music Pop Culture Arts Personal user data breached after Qld, Victoria and SA's National Park booking systems hacked Park users are being warned to keep an eye out for Queensland Parks and Wildlife staff impersonators. ( ABC News: Peter Quattrocelli ) The National Parks booking system for Queensland, Victoria and South Australia has been hacked. Queensland's environment department says it does not believe financial information has been compromised. Park users should be wary of phishing attempts. Hackers have stolen personal user information from Queensland, Victoria and South Australia's National Parks booking systems. The Queensland Department of Environment, Tourism, Science, and Innovation told 612 ABC Brisbane that the third-party provider Bookeasy had been hacked. Bookeasy processes camping and vehicle access permits for the National Parks Booking System, storing personal emails, addresses, and phone numbers. The spokesperson said "at this stage" they did not believe customers' financial information was accessed, as payments are processed through a separate system. The department spokesperson said park users should remain wary of phishing attempts by hackers impersonating national park staff. "If you receive an unexpected email, text message or phone call claiming to be from the department and asking you to confirm or provide personal information, do not respond, click on any links, or provide any personal information," the spokesperson said. "We take the privacy and security of your information extremely seriously and will provide further information to affected customers as soon as we know more." The spokesperson said any suspicious activity should be reported directly to the Queensland Parks and Wildlife Service at QPWS@detsi.qld.gov.au. A Parks Victoria spokesperson said they were aware of "suspicious Whatsapp messages" being sent to their customers. The spokesperson said they had temporarily suspended all new campsite bookings while investigations continued. "We are working urgently with Bookeasy to understand the issue and proactively communicating with our customers who may be impacted," the spokesperson said. "Existing bookings have not been cancelled and remain valid. "While we investigate, we are also temporarily unable to make changes or modifications to existing bookings." In an email, National Parks and Wildlife Service South Australia told users to remain vigilant. "Bookeasy recently detected unauthorised activity within its platform and has engaged cyber security experts to investigate," the email said. "As part of this investigation, it has been identified that some customer information, including names, contact details, and booking information, may have been accessed. "At this stage, there is no evidence that credit card details were accessed." events.title: Nvidia sinks after report implicates CEO Jensen Huang in 2nd affair
events.summary: Shares in Nvidia sank Wednesday night after the New York Times reported CEO Jensen Huang had a second affair with a senior executive who reports to him. Why it matters: The report adds to mounting scrutiny of Huang, already under investigation over an affair with a purported Chinese spy. The potential impact goes beyond one man and one business, though. Huang is arguably the world's most powerful CEO at the moment, his company serving as the beating heart of the AI revolution. He also has no obvious successor . Driving the news: Huang, 63, had a relationship with Kimberly Powell, 48, Nvidia's vice president of health care, according to the Times. Both are married to other people. The two were reportedly seen being affectionate at a hotel during Nvidia's annual developer conference in San Jose in March. A bystander recorded the interaction, and Huang's security team made an offer to the person to sign a nondisclosure agreement, per the Times. The paper reported that Nvidia declined to issue a statement, and Powell did not respond to a request for comment. By the numbers: Nvidia shares fell nearly 8% in after-hours trading as of 6 p.m. ET Wednesday. The company's lost about $1 trillion in market cap since the Times first reported on Oct. 29 that Huang had a "close relationship" with a suspected spy. On the prediction market Kalshi, the odds of Huang being out as CEO as soon as this weekend skyrocketed. Zoom out: This new report comes after Huang confirmed in a company email that he had been unfaithful in his marriage. Nvidia has an independent panel investigating, and hired the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to handle the probe. Between the lines: Peter Jaworski, a business ethics professor at Georgetown University, said it will be hard for Huang to keep his job after this. "You can't have a relationship like this with a direct report," Jaworski tells Axios. "Does the CEO get fired? In this situation that's probably the move to make." Jaworski said the situation could also raise questions about what the board knew and when it knew it. At a minimum, he says Nvidia's board needs to place Huang on administrative leave immediately while it conducts an investigation into both relationships. What we're watching: How Nvidia handles the growing scandal could have effects far beyond just its walls. Editor's note: This story has been updated with new details.

events.title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline
events.summary: Nvidia co-founder CEO Jensen Huang has never been as flashy or controversy-prone as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. Now, the 63-year-old industry kingpin has admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in an affair that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and potentially impact national security. United States officials believe that Huang’s likely romantic interest, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.) Megaspeed, a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company, had reportedly purchased $4.8 billion in Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, the Times has reported. The story took a sudden new turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of health care, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up. Separately, the Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia’s board is preparing to oust Huang , and Nvidia’s shares fell in after-hours trading. The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities. As the controversy unfolds, we are organizing the most relevant events into a reverse-chronological timeline to keep you up to date. November 11, 2026: Nvidia’s stock drops as board reportedly preps to oust CEO Jensen Huang After reports of a second extramarital affair, Nvidia’s board reportedly plans to meet to discuss Huang’s future at the company, per the Wall Street Journal. Stock fell about 8% in after hours trading on Wednesday and is down 11% in the past five days. Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has said . The company has not had an obvious successor or a succession plan. November 11, 2026: Huang also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him, NYT says The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang also had an affair with Nvidia vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell, who reports directly to the CEO. According to the report, Huang and Powell were captured on film “being affectionate” at a hotel during a conference earlier this year. November 11, 2026: Congress plans to subpoena Huang to answer questions about affair Huang has not responded to a request from three Republican congressman to appear for a closed-door briefing for questioning about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. House China committee Chairman Moolenaar said Wednesday on Fox Business that if Huang doesn’t agree to the briefing, he’ll likely be subpoenaed . November 9, 2026: Huang pulls out of various speaking engagements The Nvidia CEO pulled out of upcoming speaking engagements at the ElevenLabs Summit and Anthropic CEO Forum. November 9-10, 2026: Details emerge about the business relationships between Nvidia and the alleged spy Alice Huang and her family reportedly built a network of companies in China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, including founding a Chinese company called Shanghai Century Litong. Founded in 2023, it became an Nvidia-preferred cloud partner, giving it priority access to chips, The Information reported . The Information also reported that Shanghai Century Litong facilitated buying $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia’s chips, including banned chips. Nvidia’s head lawyer, Tim Teter, intervened in a 2025 U.S. government probe surrounding the suspected smuggling of AI chips by Megaspeed International, Bloomberg reported . Teter contacted Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler asking questions about whether the Trump administration played a role in detaining Alice Huang. In early 2025, Alice Huang and a business partner sought China-based investors for an Asian data center, promising they had no problem in securing GPUs, the Financial Times reported. November 8, 2026: Trump shows support for Nvidia CEO, calls him a “fine person” On Sunday night, President Trump weighed in on Huang’s controversy and showed support for the Nvidia CEO. “I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what’s going on,” Trump said.

events.title: Scott Colom ousts Cindy Hyde-Smith in historic Mississippi Senate flip
events.summary: Democrat Scott Colom defeated Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in a stunning Mississippi upset , becoming the first Democrat elected to the state's Senate delegation since 1982, AP projects. Why it matters: Colom's victory marks another extraordinary breakthrough for Democrats in the Deep South, extending the historic blue wave that handed the party control of both chambers of Congress. Colom also becomes Mississippi's first Black senator since Reconstruction. Hiram Rhodes Revels became the nation's first Black senator in 1870. Mississippi's last Black senator, Blanche K. Bruce, served until 1881. Catch up quick: Colom's victory expands Democrats' 55–44 advantage over Republicans in the Senate. Worries of a recount — which requires a court order, as Mississippi has no recount law — seemed moot as Hyde-Smith posted a video message to X shortly after AP called the race, appearing to concede to Colom. "While this is not the outcome we worked for or hoped for, I respect the decision of Mississippi voters. I want to congratulate Scott Cologne and wish him well as he takes on the tremendous responsibility of representing our great state," she said. Hyde-Smith also addressed another worry from Mississippi voters following a significant purge of the state's voter rolls, saying that her campaign "has worked tirelessly to ensure every legally cast vote was counted and that the people of Mississippi received a fair and transparent election." "I am proud of what we have accomplished together, but I want to make one thing very clear: an election may come to an end, but our commitment to Mississippi never will," she said. The big picture: Colom's victory followed a late surge of Democratic spending and organizing in a state Trump carried by 23 points in 2024. Hyde-Smith faced warning signs in the campaign's closing months, when Colom raised twice as much as the GOP senator despite her overall cash advantage. She was also outspent on TV advertising , with a flood of ads from left-leaning PACs and super PACs pushing support for Colom and attacking the senator for her vote not to release files related to the convicted human trafficker Jeffrey Epstein. Hyde-Smith's campaign also faced criticism over an interview she gave to WLOX-TV in Biloxi, Mississippi, where she fumbled an answer about the price of beef, saying that Mississippians had "so many other proteins to choose from." Colom's campaign capitalized on her blunder, creating a viral campaign ad urging voters to "choose another senator." The GOP made a late push to help Hyde-Smith, including President Trump speaking at a rally for her in Alcorn County, where he won by 68% in 2024. But it wasn't enough. Hyde-Smith's term will end after eight years. She was appointed to the Senate in 2018 by then-Mississippi Gov. Phil Bryant, and ran for a full term in 2020, where she bested her Democratic challenger Mike Espy by 10 points. Zoom in: Colom, a 43-year-old district attorney from Columbus, campaigned on lowering the cost of living, raising wages and protecting rural hospitals. His campaign also drew in heavy Democratic hitters to stump for him, including former President Bill Clinton, former Vice President Kamala Harris and Georgia Sen. Raphael Warnock. The bottom line: Colom's win adds Mississippi to a growing list of Republican strongholds where Democrats broke through in the midterms, including Texas and South Carolina. It also reinforces the role of Black voters in the Democratic comeback, after the party rebuilt support among a crucial voting bloc that showed signs of shifting toward Trump in 2024. Editor's note: This is a breaking news story and will be updated. This story has been corrected to show that Hyde-Smith's interview was conducted in Biloxi (not Jackson, Mississippi).

Democratic nominee Scott Colom won the Mississippi Senate election over Republican incumbent Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith , the Associated Press reported Wednesday. Colom, a local district attorney, will be the first Black senator from Mississippi since the post-Civil War Reconstruction Era. His projected victory — which was not considered likely by national analysts before Election Day — is the latest in a series of stunning wins by Democrats this midterm cycle. Two sources close to Colom's campaign said Hyde-Smith called him late Wednesday afternoon to concede. "While this is not the outcome we worked for, or hoped for, I respect the decision of Mississippi voters," Hyde-Smith said in a video posted on X . events.title: MSCI says Indonesia’s Barito Pacific will be removed from its indexes
events.summary: The latest setback comes a month after MSCI warned Indonesian stocks could be removed from its indexes next year and the market relegated to “standalone” status. MSCI will remove Barito Pacific from its indexes and move Bumi Resources Minerals to small cap, forcing index funds to sell after Nov 30. The move adds pressure on Indonesia, whose market is down over 40% in 2026 and faces a possible downgrade to “standalone” status. Authorities have tightened rules and MSCI is seeking feedback until April 30, 2027, but investors have already pulled out US$5.4 billion this year. SINGAPORE/BENGALURU - Global index provider MSCI will remove one Indonesian company from its indexes, it said on Nov 9, dealing a blow to the country’s efforts to avoid a downgrade and retain its emerging-market status. The latest setback comes a month after MSCI warned Indonesian stocks could be removed from its indexes next year and the market relegated to “standalone” status, a much harsher fate than the one the index provider first threatened in January. The deletions will force funds that track its indexes to sell the shares, and take effect after the close of trading on Nov 30. Barito Pacific will be removed from MSCI’s global standard index, while Bumi Resources Minerals will be moved from that index to the small cap index. MSCI Indonesia index currently has nine firms after the index provider culled six companies in May and two more in August. The threat of a downgrade has cast a shadow over Indonesian markets, with the benchmark index down over 40% in 2026, making it the world’s worst-performing major stock market. In October, MSCI cited Indonesia’s failure to improve ownership transparency and curb coordinated trading, turning what had been a downgrade risk to “frontier” market status into a full-blown crisis of investor confidence. The Indonesian authorities have spent much of the year trying to address MSCI’s concerns, tightening disclosure requirements and laying out plans to raise minimum free floats. In October, the regulator announced sanctions linked to alleged manipulation, while earlier this week the stock exchange removed the 5 trillion rupiah (S$353.2 million) market cap threshold for screening companies that breach high shareholding concentration rules. MSCI is seeking feedback on the reclassification proposal until April 30, 2027, and will announce its decision on or before June 30, 2027, although analysts worry that many of the active investors may exit Indonesia before that. Foreign investors have already pulled out US$5.4 billion from Indonesian equities in 2026. Goldman Sachs has estimated MSCI’s removal of the country’s stocks from its indexes could spur US$5.6 billion of passive outflows. Indonesia has been an MSCI emerging market since 1989, and a downgrade would be a huge reversal for a market that until recently was a favourite of foreign investors. More than US$1.8 trillion in assets are benchmarked to MSCI’s emerging-market indexes, according to the index provider’s website. REUTERS

events.title: Some under-25s should get less benefits, Milburn review to say
events.summary: Alan Milburn will publish his review next week Some young people could see reductions to the benefits they are entitled to, under a radical overhaul of the system to be recommended by a government-commissioned review. Alan Milburn's year-long report, which will be published on Tuesday, will recommend moving under-25s off the main sickness and disability benefits, the Times reported , external . Milburn, a former Labour health secretary, has been tasked by the government with helping reduce the one in eight 18- to 24-year-olds in the UK who are not in education, employment or training - or "Neet". He said on Wednesday night that his plans would not be "pain-free" and would affect both existing and new claimants. His report is expected to recommend that under-25s are no longer able to claim the health element of universal credit or personal independence payment (Pip). Instead, they would receive an allowance on the same basic rate as universal credit. Some could be eligible for a new "additional cost allowance" to cover day-to-day costs related to their conditions. But many claimants would receive less under the plans, which the government is set to take forward into legislation in the new year. Milburn, a Labour MP from 1992 to 2010, is also expected to recommend an investment of billions into more employment support for young people, including work placements, job subsidies and one-to-one personal advisers. Those with more severe disabilities and unable to work would get a new benefit paid at a higher rate. Speaking to the Times about his report, Milburn said: "Candidly, it could mean that some people will get less financial support at the beginning of their benefit claim than under the current system. "But actually, for young people, there's a different debate that we've got to resolve, which is whether the priority is their longer-term life chances or just their immediate shorter-term finances. "I think what the current system does [is] it prioritises the latter over the former. I believe that's the wrong choice and it needs to be the other way around." Just under one million young people in the UK are Neets , data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) from April to June suggests. This was a rise of 3% on the same period last year. Milburn's recommendations are likely to be backed by Prime Minister Andy Burnham but could prove controversial among Labour MPs, who opposed welfare reform under his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer. The reforms would represent a radical overhaul of Britain's welfare system, at a time when there is heavy political pressure for the UK to find the money to spend more on defence. If Milburn's recommendations were approved, it could take almost a decade for the British state to see monetary savings. The new system "will need significant investment" and would involve "rebuilding the system from scratch," Milburn added. He said that currently "you've got hundreds of thousands of young people stuck in a benefit system that is trapping them in poverty, giving them no prospect of prosperity or a job". His new proposed system would involve an element of carrot and stick, where young people could lose some of their benefits if they did not engage with the extra work support options. "A deal isn't a deal unless there are potential consequences," Milburn said. "Entitlements and responsibilities are two sides of the same coin." A government spokesperson said: "We will always ensure there is a safety net for the most vulnerable and those who are unable to work. "But the prime minister has been clear that we need a wholesale change in the way we support young people to grow up in this country, where we invest in their success rather than paying for failure." events.title: Nvidia tumbles as investors consider future without CEO Jensen Huang
events.summary: Nvidia’s board is reportedly preparing to oust chief executive Jensen Huang, who admitted to having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Nvidia shares fell 9% after reports raised doubts about CEO Jensen Huang’s future, with investors worried about leadership and governance. The New York Times said Huang had a relationship with a direct report, and the Wall Street Journal said the board may be preparing to oust him. Nvidia faces pressure before its Nov 17 results, as analysts say any removal could hurt client trust and force a more traditional structure. Nvidia stock sank in extended trading on Nov 11 as investors grappled with the possibility of the company without chief executiveJensen Huang at the helm. The stock began to fall in post-market trading following a New York Times report that the CEO had a relationship with a direct report. Losses extended after Wall Street Journal reported Nvidia’s board is preparing to oust Huang, who over the weekend had admitted to having a separate affair with an alleged Chinese spy. “It is going to be a very challenging situation,” said Michael O’Rourke, chief market strategist at Jonestrading. “Jensen had forecast 70% sales growth this year (2026). With the vendor financing and the aggressive tactics, his successor will spend the next year putting out fires and cleaning up messes.” He added: “If these allegations are confirmed by the independent investigation, one has to expect the board to remove him. That is the standard for corporate governance today. Even worse this is a pattern.” Other AI-linked stocks followed shares of Nvidia lower in post-market trading. Nvidia shares have been under pressure amid growing concern around the strength and longevity of the artificial intelligence trade. The chipmaker is scheduled to report quarterly results on Nov 17. It “will be interesting how it handles next week’s earnings call. Their CFO (chief financial officer) can handle the numbers but markets will want more on changes to the governance”, said Dec Mullarkey of SLC Management. “It’s hard to imagine him stepping down but also hard to imagine how he could stay on. I think the board will ultimately be forced to push him out and establish a more traditional organisational structure. The gap in judgment may be hard to repair with critical clients.” BLOOMBERG

( ABC Shepparton: Charmaine Manuel ) Victoria Police says 130 people have been arrested during a retail theft blitz in Shepparton's CBD. One offender, a 42-year-old Mooroopna woman, was arrested 21 times during the operation for supermarket shoplifting. A local business group has welcomed the police blitz but says more needs to be done to stop repeat offenders. Police say an operation targeting retail theft in Shepparton has uncovered evidence of organised offending and led to more than 200 arrests. Victoria Police launched Operation Securus in May, sending police on daily patrols through the town's shopping district to target repeat offenders after shoplifting rates reached a 10-year high . Authorities have laid more than 800 charges, whilst also uncovering a level of "organisation" behind the ongoing offending. "We're not seeing people stealing bread and milk to feed their families," Superintendent Anna Parkinson said. In May, police launched Operation Securus, focusing on retail theft in Shepparton's shopping district. ( ABC Shepparton: Charmaine Manuel ) Authorities said almost $50,000 worth of goods stolen from supermarkets, liquor stores and other shops had been returned during the operation. Police arrested 130 people, of whom about 15 per cent were repeat offenders, including a 42-year-old Mooroopna woman who had been arrested 21 times. She was subsequently sentenced to 70 days in prison. Police say 130 people have been arrested since the operation began, with some offenders arrested multiple times for shoplifting. ( ABC News ) Authorities said another theft investigation led to the seizure of drugs, including cannabis and methamphetamine, from a Shepparton property in September. Business group wants tougher bail laws Greater Shepparton Business Network vice-president Jac McCarty said the police blitz had been "fantastic" for retailers. However, she said stronger bail laws were needed to stop reoffending. "Whilst these results are pleasing, it is also disappointing to note the number of reoffenders who are being let back out to continue these behaviours," she said. Jac McCarty has welcomed the results of the operation but wants more to be done to reduce reoffending. ( Supplied: Jac McCarty ) "Our bail laws need to be strengthened to ensure real outcomes can be made." Ms McCarty said police should follow through on the promise to expand the operation beyond the Shepparton CBD later this year. "Our retailers have been threatened and left scared in their workplaces, repeat offenders are brazenly returning for more, and money is needing to be spent on security by businesses that are already fighting hardships," she said. "Crime is not just impacting the Shepparton CBD, with reports from Tatura and Mooroopna as well being quite concerning." events.title: Jensen Huang accused of having another affair — with an Nvidia exec
events.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is already under investigation after having admitted to having an affair with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy . Now the New York Times is reporting that Huang is also suspected of having another extramarital affair, with a direct report of his at the company — Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare. Like many companies, Nvidia has rules discouraging superiors from having relationships with employees in subordinate roles, the Times notes. TechCrunch reached out to Nvidia for comment. The company’s board has initiated an investigation into Huang’s publicly admitted affair. Additionally, two House Republicans said Wednesday that Congress is gearing up to subpoena Huang over the spy allegations if he doesn’t voluntarily respond to their summons to a closed-door briefing. Late Wednesday, after the reports of the second affair were published, the Wall Street Journal reported that the Nvidia board was preparing to oust Huang, who co-founded the company in 1993. events.title: Report: Nvidia preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang after affair with woman U.S. officials deemed a Chinese spy
events.summary: Nvidia’s board of directors is preparing to remove Chief Executive Jensen Huang, an ouster that would follow his admission of having an extramarital affair with a woman U.S. intelligence officials deemed to be a Chinese spy. The decision by the chipmaking giant, reported by the Wall Street Journal , would deal a swift end to Huang’s 33-year reign as CEO and promises to send shockwaves throughout the technology industry and upend America’s race in artificial intelligence. The Journal reported that Nvidia’s board could meet as soon as Wednesday to determine his fate. On Wednesday, the New York Times reported that Huang, 63 years old, had also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of health care. Powell could not immediately be reached for comment. In after-hours trading, Nvidia’s shares were down more than 7%. According to LinkedIn, Powell has been with Nvidia for nearly two decades and previously spent 10 years in AI business development. Nvidia describes her as formerly leading the company’s higher education and research business, alongside Nvidia AI labs. Huang’s long-term future with the company is not immediately clear. On Sunday, Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife, and Nvidia announced an investigation into the reports that he had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. At the time, the board said it had “no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised,” but that its inquiry would examine “all available information.” Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and has been integral to the company’s success, particularly its magnificent run in recent years. For fiscal 2026, which ended in January, the company reported revenue of $215.9 billion, up 65% over the prior year. Growth accelerated in the first half of fiscal 2027, with revenue of $96 billion, up 85% year over year. Nvidia previously guided third-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue to $108 billion, plus or minus 2%, and chief financial officer Colette Kress said the company expected 70% revenue growth in fiscal 2028. Huang reigns supreme over the company. Since its founding, he has created a unique, flat structure in which he sits at the center of most decisions, with about 60 direct reports. Nvidia’s board operates without a chair, and the company has not set out a clear succession plan. It also does not have a chief operating officer. Huang is known to text and call small clients himself. Nvidia’s succession challenge would not be whether its engineers can keep building chips without Huang, analysts say. It is whether anyone, or any leadership team, can inherit his authority to decide what gets built, secure the industry’s commitment to it, and keep customers confident in the next bet. The factors behind Huang’s potential removal “hasten a transition the company is not prepared for,” Gil Luria, an analyst with D.A. Davidson & Co., told Fortune . Nvidia’s board decision would be a forced hand. “There are rules about that; there are laws about that,” Jay Goldberg of Seaport Research Partners told Fortune , speaking about the untenability of Huang as CEO if there were internal policy violations. Nvidia won’t “go away. They’re sold out. It’s all contracted into next year, but it loses a lot of its luster. The chances of making a misstep are higher.” If Huang is ousted, the most immediate question is who will succeed him, and what sort of new plan the company will put in place to fill the vacuum of power. “Rarely has a board faced this much pressure. This is the board’s moment to shine or fade,” Michael Useem, a professor of management at the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania, told Fortune . “If the board had been doing its job, it would already have a slate of possible successors: people identified as likely successors.” Business and law experts have said Nvidia’s chief financial officer, Colette Kress, could be an option for interim CEO. Another option would be to have one of the company’s directors, such as lead independent director Stephen Neal, who is chairman emeritus and senior counsel at law firm Cooley LLP, take over as interim CEO if Huang is removed. Huang’s children and son-in-law also work at the company. Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, senior associate dean for leadership studies and Lester Crown Professor in Management Practice at Yale University’s School of Management, compared the Huang saga to what happened at McDonald’s with former CEO Steve Easterbrook, who was ousted in November 2019. The McDonald’s board investigated Easterbrook for a consensual relationship with an employee that involved the exchange of videos and romantic text messages, and then found that other undisclosed, improper relationships had occurred. Easterbrook was later charged by the SEC with making false and misleading statements to investors about the circumstances that led to his termination. Easterbrook didn’t admit or deny the findings, but agreed to a five-year officer and director bar and paid a $400,000 civil penalty. Huang’s ouster would create a massive hole for the AI industry. Huang has been central to the industry’s rapid growth. His success in creating world-leading graphics processing units, the chips that power AI by handling model training and regular user queries, has been instrumental in ushering in the AI boom and in the U.S.’s leading position. Few executives in Silicon Valley and beyond exert the level of power and influence over one company and industry. Huang’s institutional knowledge and deep industry connections have been among the reasons tech analysts and other experts have said it would be impossible to replace him. Another reason has been President Trump, who has become a close friend of Huang and stood by the executive since Sunday’s revelations, saying Huang is an “amazing guy” and “honorable man.” This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

events.title: Democrat Scott Colom wins closely watched US Senate race in Mississippi
events.summary: The historic victory flips an eighth US Senate seat for Democrats after last week’s pivotal midterm election. Democrat Scott Colom has won Mississippi’s closely watched United States Senate race, giving his party a historic victory in a Republican stronghold that has eluded them for decades. Colom, a prosecutor, will become the state’s first Black senator in more than 140 years. On Wednesday, he narrowly defeated incumbent Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith in one of the US midterms’ biggest upsets . list 1 of 3 Can Democrats shed some new light on the Epstein files when they take over? list 2 of 3 What’s delaying the US Senate election results in Mississippi and Alaska? list 3 of 3 Which key races remain undecided one week after the US midterms? The win builds on Democrats’ success after the party delivered an electoral drubbing to the rival Republicans in the November 3 midterm elections. The left-leaning party flipped at least eight US Senate seats that are currently held by Republicans. A US Senate race in Alaska remains undecided. For more than a week, the Mississippi contest was too close to call as election officials worked to count more than 100,000 mail-in ballots. Thousands of other residents who could not confirm their registration at voting sites cast provisional ballots that required confirmation of their eligibility. Colom and Hyde-Smith took markedly different approaches as remaining ballots were counted. Hyde-Smith was not seen publicly until she returned to Washington this week for the reconvening of the Senate. Through a statement, however, Hyde-Smith and her team had expressed confidence that she would win after “every legally cast vote is fully and accurately counted”. Colom, by contrast, has maintained a more public profile since the November 3 midterms. After the election, Colom held a series of events where he castigated his opponent. “Ultimately, at some point, the senator needs to speak out. Where is Cindy Hyde-Smith?” Colom told reporters on Friday in Jackson, Mississippi. “We want to hear from her. She needs to answer questions. What is her path to victory? She doesn’t have one.” The US Senate race also was not the first time the two had crossed political paths. Hyde-Smith, citing concerns about Colom’s position on transgender athletes, had previously blocked him from serving as a federal judge in 2023 after he was nominated by former US President Joe Biden. The position had required Senate approval. Colom’s win upturns political expectations for Mississippi, a state that US President Donald Trump won by just over 22 points in the 2024 presidential election. The last time a Democrat won a US Senate race in Mississippi was in 1982, when John Stennis claimed victory over Republican challenger Haley Barbour, who later became governor of the state. Colom, who has been a proponent of raising the minimum wage, increasing protections for rural hospitals and ending the US-Israel war on Iran , will be sworn in next January. The 120th Congress will include a record number of Black senators, with seven in total.

events.title: Feds arrest top official of healthcare company, alleging illegal drug importation
events.summary: U.S. authorities are accusing the two top officials of a Canadian company of operating a long-running scheme to illegally import prescription drugs into the U.S., according to court records. John Thomas Howard, treasurer and a director of the company, CANARX, was arrested Sunday on smuggling and conspiracy charges. His brother Bob Howard, CANARX president and director, is wanted in the investigation, according to records. CANARX was featured in a CNBC investigation "RiskyRX" last year that revealed how the company and others known as alternative funding programs, or AFPs, are becoming more pervasive around the U.S. as drug costs skyrocket. U.S. authorities are accusing the two top officials of a Canadian company of operating a long-running scheme to illegally import prescription drugs into the U.S., according to court records filed Tuesday. John Thomas Howard, treasurer and a director of the company, CANARX, was arrested Sunday on smuggling and conspiracy charges, according to the records. Bob Howard, his brother, who is president and a director of CANARX, is also wanted in the federal investigation, according to an affidavit from Dustin Dobbs, a special agent with the Food and Drug Administration's Office of Criminal Investigations. He has not yet been taken into custody. Besides conspiracy and smuggling, the arrest warrant said John Thomas Howard was charged with introducing misbranded drugs into interstate commerce and illegal drug importation. No plea has been filed. CANARX was featured in a CNBC investigation last year that revealed how the company and others known as alternative funding programs, or AFPs, are becoming more pervasive around the U.S. as drug costs skyrocket. The investigation found these companies have penetrated the country's healthcare system by offering high-cost specialty drugs at more affordable prices through private and public employers. In some cases, employers are requiring their staff to use an AFP. AFPs often obtain the medications overseas and ship them directly to patients, a practice that federal authorities have said is illegal and poses safety risks. CNBC traced the trail of drugs from abroad to the U.S. via a supply chain that the pharmaceutical companies producing the medications have not authorized. On its website, CANARX, founded in 2002 and based in Windsor, Ontario, Canada, described its business as the first international prescription provider for the U.S. and the safest such program in the industry. The company said it sources its medications from Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia and New Zealand. But the affidavit said that the FDA's investigation found "there is probable cause to believe that (CANARX) illegally imported or caused the illegal importation of prescription drugs into the United States …." The affidavit does not specify which medications the agency believes were illegally imported. The criminal complaint covers the period from Feb. 22, 2017, through April 15, 2026. The company's general counsel, Joseph Morris, told CNBC in a statement: "The Howards deny all the charges against them, will defend vigorously, and expect to be vindicated in court." The company has been under FDA scrutiny for several years. In 2023, the agency seized medication being shipped by CANARX that it says was potentially misbranded and counterfeit, according to an email sent to a patient that was obtained by CNBC. And in 2019, the FDA sent a warning letter to the company, saying it was operating "in a manner that substitutes the FDA-approved drugs prescribed by the U.S. healthcare provider with unapproved drugs." Morris, in response to that warning, argued CANARX was not misleading patients, but agreed for the company to stop importing drugs that need to be administered by a doctor. In an interview as part of the CNBC investigation, Morris said last year that the medicines shipped to U.S. patients come from highly regulated countries. He said CANARX was operating legally. The central question for AFPs is the legality of importing prescription drugs into the U.S. for personal use. The FDA allows Americans to import medications for individual use in some cases if the drug is not available domestically. That is the basis on which the AFPs built their models for shipping medicines directly to patients. But an FDA spokesperson told CNBC last year that "in most circumstances, a person cannot import prescription drugs from other countries into the U.S. ... as substitutes for FDA-approved drugs." In a separate civil lawsuit that is pending, Gilead Sciences accused CANARX and other companies of illegally importing Biktarvy, its medication to treat HIV. In a statement to CNBC on Wednesday, a Gilead spokesperson said the company "has taken strong legal action to protect patients and the integrity of the U.S. medicines supply chain. We welcome the government's efforts to hold accountable those whose conduct may put patients at risk." CANARX has not responded to the Gilead lawsuit.

events.summary: Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis attacked as UN appeals for urgent aid to deal with heavy rains in the enclave. Israeli attacks have killed at least nine Palestinians across Gaza, as the United Nations made an emergency appeal for waterproof tents to shelter hundreds of thousands exposed to flooding due to heavy rains. At least four Palestinians were killed in an Israeli air strike on the Nasser Medical Complex in western Khan Younis, southern Gaza in the early hours of Thursday, according to Gaza’s Civil Defence spokesperson Mahmoud Basal. list 1 of 3 Gaza’s infrastructure collapse leaves residents defenceless against floods list 2 of 3 Gaza Grad: A Palestinian-Russian family’s longing for home list 3 of 3 ‘Our neighbours are gone’: Gaza survivors recount horrors of deadly floods An Israeli air attack on Wednesday killed 38-year-old Mohammed Salem al-Daash in the al-Sabra neighbourhood, south of Gaza City. Another Palestinian was shot and killed by Israeli forces east of the al-Bureij camp in central Gaza, and another was killed in an Israeli drone strike in the al-Nasr neighbourhood, northwest of Gaza City. At least two Palestinians were killed and several others wounded in a strike targeting a tent sheltering displaced people in the Sheikh Radwan neighbourhood, north of Gaza City. Al Jazeera’s Hind Khoudary, reporting from Gaza City, described the Israeli attacks as indiscriminate targeting of civilians, saying people who were carrying on with simple attempts to survive lost their lives, such as “a man filling up a water tank, [who] was killed in a drone strike”. “In another attack, two brothers from the al-Absi family were killed while they were sheltering inside their tent on al-Jalaa Street,” she said, adding that nowhere in Gaza was safe. The Israeli attacks came as the UN appealed for more tents to be sent to the enclave because at least 70,000 tents were flooded in weekend rains, according to Gaza’s Government Media Office. Heavy rain has directly affected at least 106,000 people in Gaza in recent days, according to UNICEF, with thousands of tents for displaced Palestinians submerged under water and latrines overflowing into camps. NGOs and local organisations say they do not have the resources or capacity to deal with the crisis, as Israel continues to restrict the entry of essential aid. “Ultimately, we need the Israeli authorities to cooperate with giving the permissions so that we can bring those tents in,” UN deputy spokesperson Farhan Haq told reporters at a media briefing, adding that apart from funding, Israeli permits were needed “to get this in”. Certain countries supporting aid deliveries to Gaza say that delivering winter supplies will have to wait for the formation of an Israeli government, said Tom Fletcher, the UN under-secretary-general for humanitarian affairs. In a statement, Fletcher said foreign ministers have assured their support, “but also repeatedly said that progress would be hard until after Israeli elections. Now we’re told to wait for the formation of a government”. “This is not an acceptable excuse,” he added, citing international law and the consequences of delays, blockages and funding cuts. Italy’s Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said on Wednesday that Rome has launched a new emergency initiative worth 5 million euros ($5.5m) to provide immediate assistance to the Gaza Strip following the flooding. The death toll from the Israeli genocidal war in Gaza has surged to 74,653 civilians killed since October 7, 2023, medical sources told the Palestinian Wafa news agency on Wednesday. An additional 176,007 Palestinians have been injured in the past three years. Israel has killed 1,622 Palestinians and injured 5,878 others since the Gaza “ceasefire” agreement came into effect on October 11, 2025.

events.title: Oil rises on mixed signals over Iran war outlook
events.summary: The Iran war, which started on Feb 28, has caused gas prices to rise worldwide. Oil climbed on Nov 11, as traders weighed mixed signals on the prospects for a conclusion to the Iran war. While US President Donald Trump has said further strikes on Iran would not be necessary , regional flare-ups have persisted and peace talks have shown little progress. Iran will not remove “a single atom” of enriched nuclear material from the country, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council Mohsen Rezaee said in an interview with Al Mayadeen. West Texas Intermediate futures rose above US$86 a barrel after sliding about 5% in the previous two days, while Brent closed near US$93. “We’ve shifted from a market that needed things to get worse to move higher, to one where things simply not getting better could be enough to push prices up,” said Rebecca Babin, senior energy trader at CIBC Private Wealth Group. The US benchmark is up roughly 50% this year, but the market has reversed sharply in November, with Brent tumbling from a six-month high on hopes the conflict will ease and as Persian Gulf energy exports rise. Saudi Arabia’s crude output climbed 26% in October to the highest since the war began despite attacks on ships, as a recovery in regional flows pushes prices lower. Saudi Arabia told OPEC that its output rose to 10.56 million barrels a day in October, according to a monthly report seen by Bloomberg from the organisation’s secretariat. The bigger flows from the Saudis and other exporters around the Persian Gulf are showing up in physical markets at a time when consumption remains constrained. “We have seen a sharp re-pricing of the oil market over the past two weeks” as election results in the US and Israel “reduced the likelihood of renewed escalation in the conflict,” said Jens Naervig Pedersen, a strategist at Danske Bank AS. Still, “Iran seems hesitant to meet US demands on its nuclear programme, which may test the durability of the recent decline in oil prices.” Meanwhile, the American Petroleum Institute reported US crude inventories rose by nine million barrels last week. Stockpiles of distillates such as diesel, which had fallen below 100 million barrels for the first time since 2003, climbed by 1.5 million barrels, API said. Official data is due on Nov 12. Separately, the Energy Information Administration raised its 2027 forecasts for retail gasoline prices to an average US$3.73 a gallon and diesel to US$5.03, citing tight global fuel supplies. The agency left its US crude production estimate unchanged at 14.3 million barrels a day in its Short-Term Energy Outlook. A tanker carrying Russian diesel that had briefly signalled a US destination made a U-turn off New York, adding uncertainty over deliveries to the North American market. Last month, Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed to supply fuel to the US and global markets in a deal with Trump, though the arrangement drew criticism from Democrats. BLOOMBERG

events.title: Jensen Huang affair in D.C.: Resignation calls and moves to tighten Nvidia China exports
events.summary: The Jensen Huang affair is turning Capitol Hill into a pressure cooker, with some lawmakers calling for the country's most important tech CEO to resign amid the scandal. The situation may give Congress reason to advance a suite of bills in this year's National Defense Authorization Act to tighten export controls on advanced AI chips. What Nvidia does now — and whether Huang remains atop the company — could impact its relationship with Washington and whether lawmakers crack down. Members of Congress are calling on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to resign, and momentum is building to subpoena the executive, whose company is a leader in advanced artificial intelligence chips. Senate banking committee member Kevin Cramer , R-N.D., doubled down Wednesday on his call for Huang to resign, and a key Democratic House oversight panel member and House Republican piled on. "As a matter of his own conscience, he should resign," Cramer told CNBC, in response to revelations that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy as the chipmaker he co-founded was given permission from the U.S. government to sell its technology to China. Huang, who leads a company that's been a chief beneficiary of the artificial intelligence boom, on Sunday admitted to having an affair with a woman whom news outlets have reported U.S. intelligence concluded was a Chinese spy . The revelation is sending shockwaves through Washington, with lawmakers now fearing that U.S. AI dominance could be at risk. Is Nvidia too big to fail? Its AI financing web raises the stakes : Analysis Nvidia prepares to oust Jensen Huang, WSJ reports — stock sinks further Jensen Huang affair rocks D.C., brings calls from Congress to resign Inside Nvidia: Jensen Huang's first day in office after affair reveal Nvidia hires law firm Wachtell Lipton to lead Jensen Huang affair probe Huang affair with alleged Chinese spy complicates Nvidia China problem China panel chair Moolenaar demands answers on Nvidia CEO's alleged affair with a Chinese spy What is Megaspeed? The Nvidia chip buyer in the spotlight after Jensen Huang's affair Read Huang's email to his staff and statement from Nvidia's board of directors Nvidia's CEO turmoil gives newly empowered Democrats fresh ammunition in pursuit of oversight "What bothers me at the end of it is what we don't know is what she knows about him that can be utilized," Cramer said, referring to Alice Huang and Jensen Huang, who are not related. "This is a guy that's right now so vulnerable to extortion, blackmail. I just don't think, as a national security matter, we can run the risk." Cramer's comments come on the deadline set by a trio of House lawmakers who requested Huang to testify before their committees on Nov. 18. GOP Reps. Brian Mast, chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee; John Moolenaar, chair of the Permanent Select Committee on China; and Rick Crawford, who leads the House intelligence panel, called for Huang to appear in a Nov. 4 letter . Congress members in the majority party also have subpoena power, should they choose to use it. Mast and Moolenaar told reporters on Wednesday afternoon that they had not yet heard from Huang and that they were giving him until the end of the day to respond. Asked whether the committees were considering subpoenaing Huang if he doesn't agree to appear, Mast said "yes." Moolenaar, when asked the same question, said "all three committees have subpoena power, and I know all three committees have a very serious interest in getting to the bottom of this and having transparency around this." "We are going to continue to pursue this," Moolenaar said. The lawmakers are far from alone in their criticism, concern and outright shock over the affair. And the scrutiny is only expected to intensify with Democrats poised to take over both chambers of Congress in January. Huang has been close with President Donald Trump during the president's second term, traveling on Air Force One to China in May. "Jensen Huang should resign from Nvidia," Rep. Suhas Subramanyam, D-Va., a member of the House Oversight Committee, told CNBC. Subramanyam is the top Democrat on the panel's Subcommittee on Military and Foreign Affairs. "I didn't agree with his sentiment that there's no downside to exporting chips to China," he said. "But I never thought that he might be having an affair with a Chinese spy who was helping smuggle chips into China at an alarming rate." Rep. Don Bacon , R-Neb., who is retiring from Congress after sometimes bucking Trump, also said the CEO should step down. "From the little I know, yes." Bacon told CNBC in response to whether Huang should resign. "I mean, he allowed himself to get compromised by the Chinese government. Not good." Huang was notably opposed to strict export controls on AI chips to China, which ruffled feathers with China hawks on Capitol Hill.

events.title: Iran designates Argentinian navy, air force as ‘terrorist organisations’
events.summary: The move comes months after the government of Javier Milei designated Iran’s IRGC as a ‘terrorist organisation’. The government of Iran has announced it will designate the naval and air forces of Argentina as “terrorist organisations”, in a tit-for-tat response to how the South American country designated its Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) in March. Iran’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in a statement on Wednesday that it considers the two branches of the Argentinian military “terrorist organisations” by “the principle of reciprocity”. The statement does not mention Argentina’s army. list 1 of 3 Milei says UN ‘looking the other way’ on Falkland Islands dispute list 2 of 3 What’s the Falklands oil project at the heart of latest UK-Argentina spat? list 3 of 3 Oil production nears pre-Iran war levels, OPEC says “It is evident that the responsibility for all consequences arising from this matter will lie with the Argentine government,” the statement adds. Argentina’s foreign ministry responded with a statement of its own saying that it “categorically rejects” Iran’s designation. “This measure is completely baseless and constitutes an unacceptable accusation,” the statement reads. Wednesday’s back-and-forth, however, is not the first time that relations between Iran and Argentina have been strained. Argentina blames the Iran-backed group Hezbollah for a deadly bombing attack on the AMIA Jewish community centre in Buenos Aires in 1994, which killed 85 people and injured hundreds more. The office of Argentinian President Javier Milei referenced that incident on March 31, when it issued the “terrorist” designation against the IRGC. “President Javier Milei hopes this decision will settle a historical debt of more than 30 years with the families of the victims,” a statement from his office said at the time. “This government is determined to bring the Argentine Republic back into alignment with Western civilization, while condemning and directly combating those who seek to destroy it.” The decision to designate the IRGC as a “terrorist organisation” also aligned with a push under United States President Donald Trump to isolate Iran. The US and Israel launched a war against Iran on February 28, and the two countries have called on international allies to support their offensive. While many leaders in Latin America have avoided taking sides in global conflicts, Milei has positioned his government firmly behind the US and Israel. Milei’s abrasive style has sometimes brought him into conflict with other countries in the region, including key regional economic players like Brazil. The Argentinian leader has also revived his country’s dispute with the United Kingdom over the Falkland Islands, which his country refers to as Las Malvinas and claims as part of its national territory.

events.title: Superhuman AI bots will not steal this man's job
events.summary: News Home Just In For You Analysis Rural Watch Live Health Indigenous Politics Science Deep Time Elections World Environment Investigations Business Local news Quizzes Sport AFL NRL Football Tennis Cricket Netball Lifestyle Wellbeing Relationships & Family Food & Recipes Personal Finance Home & Garden Entertainment TV & Movies Books Music Pop Culture Arts Until superhuman swimming bots are invented, these jobs will be safe from AI Luke Gnocco is the founder of Poseidon Adventure, which operates out of Townsville and Brisbane. ( ABC News: Isabella Garrido ) Until superhuman swimming robots take his job, Luke Gnocco remains pretty relaxed about artificial intelligence (AI). "Electronics and water usually don't work," he points out. Luke Gnocco says most of his staff come from marine science backgrounds and are passionate about the reef. ( ABC News: Isabella Garrido ) Mr Gnocco's marine tourism business in north Queensland takes people on snorkelling tours on the Great Barrier Reef, jet ski tours and guided walks around Magnetic Island. He said hands-on, manual and interpersonal interactions were core aspects of the job. "With a reef tour guide, there's literally no part in the process that could be replaced by AI. Luke Gnocco says it is unlikely AI will affect hands-on jobs in the tourism industry. ( Supplied: Poseidon Adventure ) "Especially being Australia, a lot of our tourism and a lot of our products are the country, they are the reef, they are the water, and I don't think it's ever going to go backwards." While he is confident the tourism industry will weather any AI boom, recent research by public policy consultancy firm SGS Economics and Planning found about 30 per cent of work tasks across regional Queensland could be exposed to AI automation. Principal and partner Alison Holloway said regional locations were more resilient to change from AI. How India is marketing its skilled workforce to Australian businesses Developer 'pauses' AI data centre proposal after it 'misread' community feeling As Trump dismisses AI concerns, Albanese tries to show he's in control AI deepfake legislation loophole could see predators escape harsher sentences Alison Holloway says AI will affect some locations differently than others. ( Supplied: Alison Holloway ) "A lot of the knowledge jobs and professional services jobs are located in the city centres … and they're the jobs that are most exposed to AI automation," Ms Holloway said. The report found almost 40 per cent of work tasks in Brisbane were at risk of AI automation, followed by the Gold Coast on 37.1 per cent. The Sunshine Coast sits at 36.4 per cent, followed by Cairns at 36, followed by Townsville and Rockhampton at 35.6, and Mackay at 34.9. Despite the Gold Coast's status as a major tourism hub, Ms Holloway said there was a mix of occupations in the region, including many administrative tasks within tourism that were not in-person. The Gold Coast is just behind Brisbane in the number of jobs at risk of AI automation. ( ABC News: Emily Dobson ) SGS Economics and Planning drew upon research by Jobs and Skills Australia and data from the Australian Bureau of Statistics to determine the risk of exposure in different locations. Ms Holloway said roles susceptible to automation were concentrated in the professional hearts of cities, such as finance, professional services and office-based jobs. She said those less exposed to AI disruption required in-person engagement or a physical presence. SGS Economics and Planning says AI is set to disrupt how work gets done at a pace and scale few industries have faced before. ( AP: Michael Dwyer/File ) "If you think about the care economy, nursing and aged care, they're all things where a physical person is engaged in that job," she said. Christoph Breidbach, an associate professor of Business Information Systems at the University of Queensland, said many regional occupations were inherently different because they required local knowledge, human relationships or engaging with unpredictable natural environments. Dr Breidbach said farming, for example, required responding to changing weather or soil conditions and livestock behaviour. Christoph Breidbach says this time around, jobs in cities are more likely to be affected by AI than those in regional areas. ( Supplied ) "What AI does is that it could assist with planning or with scheduling or with decision support, but you simply can't replace the physical execution of these tasks, unless you have very advanced robotics," he said. While previous waves of technological change disproportionately affected regional economies, Dr Breidbach said the AI wave was different for industries like agriculture and manufacturing. "It's not so much the physical labour that is now being automated or even augmented, but you can see change to cognitive tasks. So, your writing, your analysing of information, preparing of reports, and those are tasks that you would associate with white-collar jobs.

events.title: Canada’s ambassador warns Trump tariffs are driving up costs, threatening U.S. investment
events.summary: Canada’s ambassador to the U.S., Mark Wiseman, warned that uncertainty surrounding President Donald Trump’s tariffs is raising investment costs and discouraging businesses from expanding. New York Fed research found that roughly 90% of tariff costs were passed on to U.S. importers, with additional consumer price pressures expected in 2027. Canada is seeking to attract investment with a lower effective business tax rate, as trade tensions persist and Democrats prepare to challenge Trump’s tariffs in Congress. Canada's ambassador to the U.S. warned Wednesday that President Donald Trump's tariffs are driving up investment costs and discouraging business expansion, as new Federal Reserve research points to more price hikes for American consumers next year. "Uncertainty increases your cost of capital," Ambassador Mark Wiseman said at the B20 summit , a gathering of global business leaders in Washington hosted by the U.S. Chamber of Commerce. "If you're going to build a new plant, add a new ship, spend money on R&D, the more certainty you have, the more likely you're going to do that," said Wiseman, a former BlackRock executive who became Canada's ambassador in February. His warning comes as Washington and Ottawa struggle to resolve a tariff quarrel affecting one of the U.S.'s largest trading relationships. The two countries exchanged roughly $570 billion in goods during the first nine months of 2026, according to U.S. Census Bureau data . That's an increase from the same period in 2025, the first year of Trump's second term, but lower than the comparable nine months during the previous three years, when Joe Biden was president. U.S. customs duties calculated on imports from Canada reached $10 billion in 2025, compared with $400 million in 2024, according to the Congressional Research Service . An October study by New York Fed researchers found that nearly 90% of tariff costs were passed on to U.S. importers, with about a quarter of tariff increases eventually reaching consumer goods prices and further price pressures expected in 2027. The findings come as Labor Department data showed consumer prices rose a higher-than-expected 0.4% in October, adding to inflation concerns after Republicans' sweeping midterm losses . Trump has defended his tariffs as necessary to protect U.S. manufacturers and workers, accusing Canada of discriminatory trade practices that disadvantage U.S. exporters. The two governments have resumed negotiations after talks collapsed in August, with discussions focused on reducing tariffs on Canadian steel and automobiles. Trump has imposed duties of up to 50% on certain Canadian products , prompting retaliatory measures targeting billions of dollars in U.S. exports. Wiseman called for the removal of tariffs imposed under Sections 232 and 338 of U.S. trade law, saying a resolution would help businesses make long-term investment decisions. The political stakes have shifted following the midterms, with Democrats preparing to challenge Trump's tariffs when they take control of Congress in January. Still, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Tuesday that the Trump administration remains Canada's principal negotiating partner. "We've had comprehensive free trade with the United States since 1988," Wiseman said, describing Canada's objective as returning "as close as we can to free trade" while creating the certainty businesses need. European ambassadors echoed those concerns at the B20 summit. Germany's ambassador to the U.S., Jens Hanefeld, said businesses could adapt to tariffs but struggled with an "ever-changing regulatory environment" that forced companies to spend more on lawyers to navigate shifting trade rules. Speaking on the same panel, France's ambassador, Aurélien Lechevallier, urged greater cooperation on AI and energy rather than continued trade disputes. "We've spent, I think, a lot of time the last years working and dealing with regulations, tariffs," he said. "Businesses are eager to do more business."
